Hi Raj / Sara,

Thanks again for the time earlier — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the workload. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned before we hand things over to benchmarking: 

Summary of what I heard from you:
- Target latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 150ms for short replies (<= 128 tokens).
- Throughput goal: sustained 500 RPS (concurrent traffic pattern) with bursts up to ~1k RPS.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrency ~60-80 users; plan for 100 headroom.
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required for your UX (clients render as tokens arrive).
- Model family: preference for an Llama-variant compatible with quantization; will confirm exact model after procurement.

Attached I'm sharing the initial materials we'll use for the benchmark: prompt set (edgefin_prompt_set_v2.csv), harness configuration (harness_config.yml), and a short measurement definitions doc (measurement_definitions.md).

What we'll do next (proposed):
1) You review the prompt set and confirm the distribution looks representative (short/medium/long buckets).
2) We run an initial lab run with 10-minute steady-state windows to validate baseline latency and streaming behavior.
3) We iterate on batching/quantization profile and then run a 1-hour soak to validate throughput and p95 objectives.
4) Share reproducible harness config + Dockerfile + raw measurement logs and analysis.

Please confirm the targets above (esp. p95 and concurrency) and let us know any constraints for the lab (e.g., we should test against a private VPC, or use your test dataset). If that all looks good I'll schedule an engineering sync with Rishi and Priyom for next week and kick off the first run.

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications / asks from our side before the lab run: 

- Confirmed targets: p95 <= 150ms (short replies), steady throughput 500 RPS with bursts to 1k.
- Concurrency: our internal load tests show peaks around 75 concurrent active writers; 100 headroom is fine.
- Streaming: yes, we need chunked partial-token streaming (client shows partial output as it arrives). That means the benchmark should measure first-byte and token-stream latency separately from final completion p95.
- Reproducibility: very important for our procurement/security team. We'll need the exact harness (Dockerfile + versions), seed/prompt configs, and raw logs for audit. We may ask security to run an independent verification.

Couple of questions: 
1) In the prompt set I saw ~12% of prompts are long-context (>512 tokens) — do you suggest we split runs and report both short/long breakout metrics?
2) Can Redwood provide a quantization matrix (FP16/INT8/...) options and expected latency/cost tradeoffs for the suggested model?

If this is all doable, Sara and I are happy to join the engineering sync next week. Can we do Tue 6/30 or Wed 7/1? Prefer Tue am PT.

Best,

Raj — thanks for the quick reply and great questions. Quick answers inline and a bit more detail on measurement defs below.

1) Prompt buckets: yes, we will split the runs and report short (<=128 tokens), medium (129-512), and long (>512) buckets separately. For the initial pass we'll focus on the short/medium mix that matches your traffic (I adjusted the attached prompt_set_v2 to mirror the ~12% long that you flagged).

2) Quantization options: we support FP16, 4-bit and 8-bit quantized variants depending on the model. In our internal tests the typical latency deltas are:
   - FP16: baseline accuracy, higher memory and latency
   - INT8 (8-bit): ~10-20% latency improvement, slight accuracy shift on worst-case prompts
   - Q4 (4-bit): ~30-50% latency improvement, requires careful eval sets for quality regression
We'll include the exact quantization matrix and the benchmark profiles in the repo.

Measurement definitions (short):
- First-byte latency: time from request send until first data frame arrives (for streaming).
- Token-stream latency: distribution of inter-token arrival times once the first byte is sent.
- Completion latency (p50/p90/p95/p99): end-to-end time to final token.
- Throughput: sustained completed responses per second, measured in 5-minute steady-state windows. We report also percentile drops during bursts.
- Reproducibility: all harness artifacts (Dockerfile, harness_config.yml, prompt_set, seed values) + raw logs and an instruction to re-run the identical job with the same seed. We also publish an evaluation script that computes the metrics from raw traces.

Re: streaming, we'll capture first-byte and token-stream metrics as separate series in the output CSV so you can validate UX rendering constraints.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the Tuesday 6/30 9:30am PT slot? I'll invite Rishi and Priyom.
- Please confirm whether the initial run should be against a Redwood-hosted lab (public endpoint) or your VPC. If VPC, we'll need firewall/test network details and an engineer on your side to enable connectivity.

Hi Raj / team — Rishi from infra here, jumping in on the technical plan. Appreciate the earlier notes — a few engineering-level clarifications so the bench outputs are actionable for ops: 

1) Environment: please run both (a) Redwood-hosted lab (standard config) and (b) a VPC-local run if you want the lowest-network-variance numbers. For procurement we'll provide both but mark the VPC run as "production-proximate."

2) Steady-state windows: measure throughput and completion p95 over non-overlapping 5-minute windows across a 60-minute soak. Report the median 5-minute window and worst-case 5-minute window across the hour. This reduces jitter noise.

3) Streaming metrics: we'll capture first-byte and per-token inter-arrival percentiles (p50/p90/p95). For streaming UX, recommend we capture the 95th percentile first-token time as the primary "perceived latency" metric.

4) Harness config: in harness_config.yml we will pin: curl/htop/gcc versions, python version, the exact model artifact SHA, and the container runtime (runc/containerd). Please ensure the Dockerfile pins the base image digest so the run is deterministic.

5) Reproducibility: We'll publish a "repro-run.sh" that replays the same request trace (timestamps + seed) against the same model artifact and outputs a deterministic metrics CSV. That will be the artifact for your security team.

Action items for EdgeFin: please share a short sample distribution of prompts (CSV row sample is fine) and confirm whether the VPC test is possible. Also confirm Tue 6/30 9:30am PT for an eng-to-eng sync.

Thanks — will be on the call if scheduled.
